title: AI Risk Categorization Decoded (AIR 2024): From Government Regulations to Corporate Policies
measurement_description: The paper constructs a comprehensive AI risk taxonomy (AIR 2024) by analyzing government regulations and corporate policies. In terms of faith/religion, it identifies and categorizes risks related to 'Hate Speech' and 'Discrimination/Bias' targeting 'Religion' and 'Beliefs' as protected characteristics. It also identifies specific region-dependent risks such as 'Undermining religious policies', 'Promoting cults', and 'Promoting feudal superstitions' (specifically in Chinese regulations and policies). The study measures the presence and specificity of these risk categories within the acceptable use policies and terms of service of major AI companies.
findings: The paper includes 'Religion' and 'Beliefs' as standard protected characteristics under Discrimination/Bias and Hate Speech categories in its AIR 2024 taxonomy. It finds that Chinese regulations and company policies (e.g., Baidu, DeepSeek) include unique religion-related risk categories not found in US or EU policies, specifically 'Undermining religious policies', 'Promoting cults', and 'Promoting feudal superstitions'. The study notes that while most companies cover general hate speech and discrimination, the specificity regarding religious risks varies by jurisdiction.
